newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - December 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - December 18.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Wednesday's edition of Daily Variety:
NEW YORK - NBC has reasserted its primetime dominance in the Dec. 5-12 Nielsen results, taking the week by a hefty 5 shares in adults 18-49 and 25-54 categories.

HOLLYWOOD - Clark Gable's 1934 Oscar for It Happened One Night has found its way home to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts & Sciences with the help of Steven Spielberg. The film maker, who anonymously purchased the award at an auction Sunday for $607,500, has presented the statuette to the Academy Foundation, which will place it on permanent display at the Academy's Center for Motion Picture Study.

HOLLYWOOD - On the same day he announced he was re-upping with Showtime for four more years, the Viacom -owned pay network's programming president, Jerry Offsay, unveiled a new slate of original films in various stages of production and development that feature such veteran performers as Hume Cronyn, Ben Kingsley, Jack Lemmon, James Earl Jones and Karl Malden.

SYDNEY - The foreign box office looks set to end the year on a record high, with three films (Fox's Independence Day, Paramount's Mission: Impossible, Universal's Twister) grossing over $200 million, compared to only one (Die Hard With A Vengeance) in 1995.

HOLLYWOOD - Producers Chuck Fries and Dick Berg will be bringing novelist Elmore Leonard's original screenplay American Flag to the big screen. Among his more than 30 novels, Leonard has had Get Shorty, Fifty-Two Pick-Up and Hombre turned into feature films.

HOLLYWOOD - They're tired of it: press kits with little or no info on the writer. Film synopses that don't credit scribes. Even press junkets that exclude screenwriters but include a film's dog performers. Continuing a campaign launched earlier this year to improve the writers' image, the Writers Guild of America has taken on the outside publicity firm of Clein & White.
